active coordinate in \eqref{eq:target-caus-normal-form} relative to the generated
coboundary space, return graph, and target kernel.  The finite evaluator
computes certified enclosures for
\(H_\Sigma^{\Caus},S_\Sigma^{\Caus},\beta_\Sigma^{\Caus},
\delta_\Sigma^{\rm cyc},\Psi_\Sigma^{\Caus}\), and
\(\operatorname{Gc}_\Sigma^{\Caus}\).  Directed structure is absent from
singular formation exactly when
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:caus-absence-criterion}
 H_\Sigma^{\Caus}=S_\Sigma^{\Caus}
 =\operatorname{Gc}_\Sigma^{\Caus}=0
\end{equation}
and every retained resolvent input--output matrix element vanishes.
For a nonzero class, \(\beta_\Sigma^{\Caus}<1\) gives strict carrier
passivity, positive \(\delta_\Sigma^{\rm cyc}\) gives infinite recurrent
physical charge, and zero cycle price constructs the next target-aligned
return support.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The closed coboundary quotient, its total preimage graph, the recurrent
support graph, graph boundary, and target kernel form the ordered typed
partition in \eqref{eq:target-caus-normal-form}.  Signed gluing precedes all
these projections.  The sharp radius is the order domination problem of
\cref{thm:target-aligned-carrier-duality}; cycle price is
\cref{thm:target-current-circulation-duality}; and resolvent variations
factor through the same source by \cref{prop:nonnormal-source-invariance}.
Their finite primal--dual programs and
\cref{thm:stagewise-target-core-computation} compute the stated intervals.
Criterion \eqref{eq:caus-absence-criterion}, together with zero compressed
response, deletes every directed incidence path.  Conversely a nonzero
coordinate supplies its path and signed support.  The final alternatives are
the passivity and circulation dualities.
\end{proof}

\section{Target-aligned quotient and constraint normal form}
\label{sec:continuum-abs-normal-form}

\begin{definition}[Quotient horizontal--vertical normal form]
\label{def:target-abs-normal-form}
Let \(q:X\to Q\) be a generated constraint, gauge, or coarse quotient, with
pullback \(U\), generated averaging/right inverse \(P\), and totalized
projection \(\Pi_q=UP\).  For a public current \(J\), put
\[
 J_Q=PJU,
 \qquad E_q=JU-UJ_Q.
\]
On the ordinary graph the target-aligned quotient identity is
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:target-abs-normal-form}
 J=UJ_QP+E_qP+J(I-\Pi_q).
\end{equation}
The first term is horizontal descent, the second is the intertwining defect,
and the third is vertical/fiber motion.  If an operation in this identity is
nonordinary, the ordered totalization replaces the identity by the typed
record
\[
 \operatorname{NF}_{\Abs}(J;q)
 :=(UJ_QP,E_qP,J(I-\Pi_q),J_q^{\rm coker},J_q^{\rm gc}),
\]
where \(J_q^{\rm coker}\) is the target-visible
failure of generated lifting or surjectivity, and \(J_q^{\rm gc}\) is the
first nonordinary quotient, constraint, gauge, or pressure graph value.
Each term is projected to the target incidence core after its ancestry is
fixed.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Quotient formation invariants]
\label{def:target-abs-formation-invariants}
Define
\begin{align}
 A_{\Sigma}^{\rm desc}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma E_qP\|_{\rm red},
 &A_{\Sigma}^{\rm vert}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J(I-\Pi_q)\|_{\rm red},
 \label{eq:abs-descent-vertical-invariants}\\
 A_{\Sigma}^{\rm coker}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J_q^{\rm coker}\|_{\rm red},
 &A_{\Sigma}^{\rm gc}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J_q^{\rm gc}\|_{\rm red},
 \label{eq:abs-cokernel-graph-invariants}\\
 A_{\Sigma}^{\rm tgt}(C)
 &:=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda_{\Sigma,\mathfrak b}}
       \|\lambda-\lambda\circ\Pi_q\|_{\rm ou,*},
 \label{eq:abs-target-descent-invariant}\\
 \operatorname{Cap}_{\Sigma}^{\ker q}(C)
 &:=\inf\{\mathcal E(v):v\in\ker q,
            \langle\lambda,v\rangle=1\},
 &\operatorname{Rank}_{\Sigma}(q;C)
 &:=\dim_{\rm cyl}\operatorname{span}
   \{\lambda\circ U\}_{\lambda\in\mathscr C^\infty}.
 \label{eq:abs-capacity-rank-invariants}
\end{align}
At finite depth, \(\dim_{\rm cyl}\) is the rank of the rational pairing
matrix; the limiting rank is its monotone generated value.
The quotient formation tuple is
\[
 \mathfrak I_{\Sigma}^{\Abs}
 :=(A_{\Sigma}^{\rm desc},A_{\Sigma}^{\rm vert},
 A_{\Sigma}^{\rm coker},A_{\Sigma}^{\rm gc},A_{\Sigma}^{\rm tgt},
 \operatorname{Cap}_{\Sigma}^{\ker q},\operatorname{Rank}_{\Sigma}(q)).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exhaustion and measurement of quotient singular structure]
\label{thm:continuum-abs-normal-form-exhaustion}
Every target-aligned \(\Abs\)-headed atomic component has exactly one first active value
in the ordered typed record extending \eqref{eq:target-abs-normal-form}.
The finite incidence and moment
hierarchies compute the four reduced current-defect norms, the target-descent
defect, kernel capacity, and target rank.  Quotient structure is absent from singular formation exactly
when
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:abs-absence-criterion}
 A_{\Sigma}^{\rm desc}=A_{\Sigma}^{\rm vert}
 =A_{\Sigma}^{\rm coker}=A_{\Sigma}^{\rm gc}
 =A_{\Sigma}^{\rm tgt}=0
\end{equation}
---equivalently, the current defects vanish and every retained target
covector descends through \(q\).  On this cell the horizontal
term transfers the problem to \(Q\) without creating a source.  Every nonzero
invariant gives the corresponding intertwining, vertical, cokernel, or graph
successor with its original source ancestry.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Insert \(I=\Pi_q+(I-\Pi_q)\) on the right of \(J\), then add and subtract
\(UJ_QP\).  Totalization of \(U,P,q\), and their range graphs supplies the
cokernel and graph terms, proving exhaustiveness.  Rational pairing matrices
compute finite ranks; the remaining quantities are norms or constrained
energy minima in the Archimedean cylinder algebra and hence have the stated
enclosures.  Under \eqref{eq:abs-absence-criterion}, all vertical,
target-descent, and failed descent paths are target-null, so only exact
horizontal descent remains.
Conversely each nonzero block is detected by its defining target covector and
therefore supplies a proper incidence edge.
\end{proof}

\section{Target-aligned lift, scale, and compactness normal form}
\label{sec:continuum-lift-normal-form}

\begin{definition}[Continuum Lift normal form]
\label{def:target-lift-normal-form}
Fix the canonical evaluation compactification and a generated lift or chart
\((\Omega,\pi,\Lambda)\), with fiber averaging \(P_\kappa\) and
\(\Pi_\pi=UP_\kappa\).  Let \(J^\Omega\) denote the total current in the
lifted presentation.  On the ordinary lift graph, the first three
coordinates satisfy the exact identity
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:target-lift-normal-form}
 J^\Omega=UJ_XP_\kappa+E_\pi P_\kappa
  +J^\Omega(I-\Pi_\pi).
\end{equation}
They are base transport, lift-intertwining defect, and within-fiber motion.
The ordinary base term retains the head of \(J_X\); the second and third
terms are \(\Lift\)-headed and retain the base ancestry.
The complete ordered typed record is
\[
 \operatorname{NF}_{\Lift}(J^\Omega;\pi)
 :=(UJ_XP_\kappa,E_\pi P_\kappa,J^\Omega(I-\Pi_\pi),
    J_{\rm conc},J_{\rm osc},J_{\rm sc}^{\rm coh},J_{\rm chart}^{\rm gc}).
\]
Its next two coordinates are the concentration and oscillation
coordinates of the fixed graph-complete compactification.  The sixth is the
nonexact scale/modulation cohomology after covariant carrier conjugation, and
the last is the first nonordinary chart, scaling, product, localization, or
realization value.  Tail and terminal descendants are transferred to the
\(\Bdry\) normal form after retaining their \(\Lift\) ancestry.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lift and compactness formation invariants]
\label{def:target-lift-formation-invariants}
Define
\begin{align}
 L_{\Sigma}^{\rm int}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma E_\pi P_\kappa\|_{\rm red},
 &L_{\Sigma}^{\rm fib}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J^\Omega(I-\Pi_\pi)\|_{\rm red},
 \label{eq:lift-interface-fiber-invariants}\\
 L_{\Sigma}^{\rm conc}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J_{\rm conc}\|_{\rm var},
 &L_{\Sigma}^{\rm osc}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J_{\rm osc}\|_{\rm var},
 \label{eq:lift-concentration-oscillation-invariants}\\
 L_{\Sigma}^{\rm sc}(C)&:=\|[J_{\rm sc}]\|_{\rm red},
 &L_{\Sigma}^{\rm gc}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J_{\rm chart}^{\rm gc}\|_{\rm red}.
 \label{eq:lift-scale-graph-invariants}
\end{align}
The variation norms are computed on the countable cylinder algebra of the
fixed compactification.  The scale valuation \(\kappa_P\) and record-scale
velocity \(a=\dot r/r\) are retained as coordinates of
\(L_\Sigma^{\rm sc}\).
The lift formation tuple is
\[
 \mathfrak I_{\Sigma}^{\Lift}
 :=(L_{\Sigma}^{\rm int},L_{\Sigma}^{\rm fib},
 L_{\Sigma}^{\rm conc},L_{\Sigma}^{\rm osc},
 L_{\Sigma}^{\rm sc},L_{\Sigma}^{\rm gc}).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exhaustion and measurement of compactness structure]
\label{thm:continuum-lift-normal-form-exhaustion}
Relative to the fixed continuum presentation, every target-visible
\(\Lift\)-headed weak limit, concentration, oscillation, defect measure,
chart degeneration, blow-up profile, and scale escape has a unique first active coordinate in the
ordered typed record extending \eqref{eq:target-lift-normal-form}.  The six invariants in
\cref{def:target-lift-formation-invariants} are computed by monotone
cylinder-variation and ordered moment enclosures.  Lift/compactness structure
is absent from singular formation exactly when all six vanish and the base
term descends ordinarily.  Otherwise the least nonzero invariant explicitly
identifies the interface, fiber, concentration, oscillation, scale, or graph
mechanism used by the target-active cascade.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The first three terms are the exact lift identity obtained by inserting
\(UP_\kappa\).  Sourcewise graph completion splits failure of strong
compactness into the ordinary weak value, its positive concentration
coordinate, its signed oscillation/polarization coordinate, and the first
nonordinary operation value.  These coordinates are unique relative to the
fixed canonical evaluation compactification.  Covariant production valuation
then separates exact scale coboundaries from the scale cohomology class.
This proves exhaustiveness.  Total variation on a countable cylinder algebra
is the supremum over finite rational partitions, and the remaining norms are
ordered cylinder programs; hence the finite hierarchy computes all six.
Their simultaneous vanishing deletes every nonbase lift incidence path.
Every nonzero value carries its detecting covector and produces the stated
successor.
\end{proof}

\section{Target-aligned boundary and terminal normal form}
\label{sec:continuum-bdry-normal-form}

\begin{definition}[Oriented boundary normal form]
\label{def:target-bdry-normal-form}
Let \(\mathscr K\) be a finite target-retaining carrier complex.  Sum its
cellwise Stieltjes identities with their orientations.  The boundary current
has the canonical decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:target-bdry-normal-form}
 J^{\Bdry}
 =\partial_{\rm int}\mathscr K
  +J_{\rm ext}+J_{\rm tail}+J_{\rm term}+J_{\rm tr}^{\rm gc}.
\end{equation}
Paired internal faces constitute \(\partial_{\rm int}\mathscr K\) and cancel
identically.  The remaining terms are exterior physical flux, compactified
tail flux, continuation/terminal-shell flux, and the first nonordinary trace,
exhaustion, overlap, boundary-condition, or terminal-realization value.
Faces at intersections are assigned by the fixed half-open priority
\[
 \mathrm{terminal}\ \succ\ \mathrm{tail}\ \succ\ \mathrm{exterior};
\]
equivalently, use the corresponding inclusion--exclusion strata.  Hence a
corner is counted once while retaining every incident ancestry label.
Killing or support loss is the zero terminal-value specialization of
\(J_{\rm term}\).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boundary formation invariants]
\label{def:target-bdry-formation-invariants}
Define
\begin{align}
 B_{\Sigma}^{\rm ext}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J_{\rm ext}\|_{\rm var},
 &B_{\Sigma}^{\rm tail}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J_{\rm tail}\|_{\rm var},
 \label{eq:bdry-exterior-tail-invariants}\\
 B_{\Sigma}^{\rm term}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J_{\rm term}\|_{\rm var},
 &B_{\Sigma}^{\rm gc}(C)&:=\|\Pi_\Sigma J_{\rm tr}^{\rm gc}\|_{\rm red},
 \label{eq:bdry-terminal-graph-invariants}\\
 \operatorname{TailCap}_\Sigma(C)
 &:=\inf\{\mathcal E(v):v|_{\partial_\infty}=1
       \text{ on a retained tail shell}\}.
 \label{eq:bdry-tail-capacity}
\end{align}
All fluxes are measured after internal-face cancellation.  A positive
exterior flux is physical expenditure only when the public carrier identity
dominates it.
The boundary formation tuple is
\[
 \mathfrak I_{\Sigma}^{\Bdry}
 :=(B_{\Sigma}^{\rm ext},B_{\Sigma}^{\rm tail},
 B_{\Sigma}^{\rm term},B_{\Sigma}^{\rm gc},
 \operatorname{TailCap}_{\Sigma}).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exhaustion and measurement of boundary singular structure]
\label{thm:continuum-bdry-normal-form-exhaustion}
Every target-aligned \(\Bdry\)-headed atomic component belongs uniquely to the exterior,
tail, terminal, or graph block of \eqref{eq:target-bdry-normal-form} after
internal cancellation.  The finite exhaustion, trace, carrier, and capacity
programs compute certified enclosures for the five invariants in
\cref{def:target-bdry-formation-invariants}.  Boundary structure is absent
from singular formation exactly when
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:bdry-absence-criterion}
 B_{\Sigma}^{\rm ext}=B_{\Sigma}^{\rm tail}
 =B_{\Sigma}^{\rm term}=B_{\Sigma}^{\rm gc}=0.
\end{equation}
A nonzero exterior invariant is charged or returned as a \(\Bdry\)
successor; a nonzero tail invariant generates its exhaustion/compactification
successor; and a nonzero terminal invariant realizes target contact only
through the totalized terminal-flux graph.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The cellular boundary identity cancels every oppositely oriented common
face.  The fixed half-open priority partitions the remaining faces into
disjoint exterior, compactification-tail, and terminal strata; the
inclusion--exclusion identity preserves their signed sum.  Totalization
supplies the graph block.  Jordan decomposition on these disjoint supports
gives uniqueness.  Variation is computed by finite
rational partitions, capacity by its Dirichlet primal--dual program, and
graph values by the ordered hierarchy.  Criterion
\eqref{eq:bdry-absence-criterion} annihilates every boundary incidence path.
The three nonzero routes follow from carrier admission, exhaustion
totalization, and the killed-flux realization law.
\end{proof}

\section{The continuum singularity-formation profile}
\label{sec:continuum-formation-profile}

\begin{definition}[The thirty-one target-aligned formation cells]
\label{def:continuum-formation-profile}
For each nonempty support \(A\subseteq\Channels\), let
\(\mathscr C_A(E)\) be the graph-complete compact closure of the union of
normalized same-origin target cells in the minimal realization with exact
source support \(A\) and physical ceiling \(E\).  Ordinary path values,
first nonordinary realization values, and their origin tags remain distinct
coordinates of this closure.  Its atomic invariant vector is
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:atomic-continuum-formation-vector}
 \mathbf I_A^\Sigma
 :=\bigoplus_{c\in A}\mathfrak I_{\Sigma}^{c}\big|_{\mathscr C_A(E)},
\end{equation}
where the five summands are the invariant tuples in
\cref{def:target-geometric-formation-invariants,%
def:target-caus-formation-invariants,%
def:target-abs-formation-invariants,%
def:target-lift-formation-invariants,%
def:target-bdry-formation-invariants}.  Adjoin the aggregate signed carrier
class, recurrent cycle price, same-origin realization graph, and cofinal shell
coordinate.  The resulting compact invariant image is the
\emph{formation profile}
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:continuum-formation-profile}
 \mathfrak F_A^\Sigma(E)
 :=\overline{\left\{
  (\mathbf I_A^\Sigma,[H]_A,\delta_A^{\rm cyc},
   \mathbf R,\operatorname{Shell}_\Sigma):
  C\in\mathscr C_A(E)\right\}}.
\end{equation}
Scalar valuation coordinates take values in their order compactifications
\([0,\infty]\); graph and measure coordinates use the compact topologies
already fixed by the minimal realization.  Hence the closure in
\eqref{eq:continuum-formation-profile} is taken in a specified compact
product, not in an implicit norm topology.
A coordinate is a \emph{detector} when its vanishing is part of the
corresponding absence criterion.  Thus capacity, resistance, rank,
domination radius, and cycle price are valuations of a detected mechanism,
not detectors by themselves.  Let \(\mathbf D_A^\Sigma\) denote the
subvector consisting of
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &(G^{\Geom},\operatorname{Ker}^{\Geom},\operatorname{Gc}^{\Geom}),\\
 &(H^{\Caus},S^{\Caus},\Psi^{\Caus},\operatorname{Gc}^{\Caus}),\\
 &(A^{\rm desc},A^{\rm vert},A^{\rm coker},A^{\rm gc},A^{\rm tgt}),\\
 &(L^{\rm int},L^{\rm fib},L^{\rm conc},L^{\rm osc},L^{\rm sc},L^{\rm gc}),\\
 &(B^{\rm ext},B^{\rm tail},B^{\rm term},B^{\rm gc})
\end{aligned}
\]
for the sources belonging to \(A\).
A profile point is \emph{realized} when its origin and total-graph rows
diagonally reconstruct a public solution path.  It is \emph{formation
active} when its normalized shell coordinate is nonzero and at least one
coordinate of \(\mathbf D_A^\Sigma\) or the aggregate feeding/storage class
is nonzero.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Continuum target-aligned structural exhaustion]
\label{thm:continuum-target-structure-exhaustion}
On every nonempty ordinary finite physical stratum,
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:contact-formation-profile-equivalence}
 \boxed{\begin{gathered}
 \Reach_\Sigma^{\Phys}(E)>0\\
 \Longleftrightarrow\
 \exists\,\varnothing\ne A\subseteq\Channels:
 \mathfrak F_A^\Sigma(E)
 \text{ contains a realized}\\[-1mm]
 \text{formation-active point}.
 \end{gathered}}
\end{equation}
There are exactly \(2^5-1=31\) possible named nonempty supports; a particular
equation may realize fewer of them.  Within each cell, the five
normal-form theorems give an exhaustive atomic word after the fixed
projection order
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:continuum-normal-form-order}
 \Geom\longrightarrow\Caus\longrightarrow\Abs
 \longrightarrow\Lift\longrightarrow\Bdry,
\end{equation}
Within one source family the first nonzero typed coordinate is unique.
Different source families may remain simultaneously active and are retained
by \(A\), the aggregate carrier class, and the circulation graph.  No sixth
target-bearing family exists.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On a cofinal approach-contact branch, contact gives a disjoint unit-increment
shell cascade.  Finite support exhaustion selects one nonempty \(A\) on a
subsequence.  On a terminal-entry branch, the completed shell graph instead
gives a \(\Bdry\)-headed owner and the terminal-entry coordinate; take its
exact provenance support as \(A\).  Target-incidence compression retains
precisely these source--shell paths.  Apply the five
normal-form theorems in the order
\eqref{eq:continuum-normal-form-order}; every headed ordinary or nonordinary
atomic component enters exactly one block, while composite ancestry and
signed interactions remain in the exact support, aggregate carrier, and
circulation coordinates.  On a finite current record the affine shell
identity supplies a positive component; on a variation-boundary record the
closed owner supplies it.  The resulting profile is formation active.
Same-origin diagonal realization gives the required profile point.

Conversely, a realized formation-active point includes a public same-origin
path and nonzero cofinal shell coordinate.  Its shell coordinate therefore
crosses every retained neighborhood of the complete continuation target,
which is contact.  The universal provenance theorem and
\cref{thm:no-additional-continuum-singularity-source} place every ordinary,
defective, or limiting shell-current occurrence in one of these cells.
Since \(J_{\Res}\subseteq\Null_\Sigma\), no additional target-bearing family
remains.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Direct target-local invariant refinement]
\label{thm:direct-continuum-invariant-protocol}
For each rational \(E>0\), support \(A\), and refinement depth \(n\), the
following finite target-local procedure constructs a joint outer
approximation to the formation profile.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)}]
\item Generate the first \(n\) forward source words and backward shell
covectors, retain their conservative incidence core, and form the saturated
cumulative join with every earlier prefix.  Discard all coordinates outside
that joint source--target incidence core.
\item Apply the five canonical normal-form projections in
\eqref{eq:continuum-normal-form-order}.  Store every zero identity and every
typed first nonordinary or graph-boundary value.
\item Solve the finite rational primal--dual programs defining the atomic
invariants, aggregate carrier radius, cycle price, and realization rows.
\item Return a nested finite union of rational product boxes
\(\mathfrak F_{A,n}^\Sigma(E)\) containing the joint invariant, origin, and
total-realization image.  Preserve all finite correlations imposed by the
ordered rows, and refine the least target-visible coordinate whose
zero/nonzero or ordinary/nonordinary status can change formation activity.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:formation-profile-computation}
 \mathfrak F_{A,n}^\Sigma(E)\downarrow
 \mathfrak F_A^\Sigma(E).
\end{equation}
If every support cover loses formation activity at a finite depth, the stored
identities concatenate to a finite regularity derivation.  Otherwise every
compatible nested word determines a graph-complete joint profile.  Apply
\cref{thm:continuum-composition-no-creation} before its realization row.  A
least unprocessed limiting target increment has a finite joint-prefix witness
and is fed back as the next five-channel successor.  A target-null joint limit
closes.  Every cumulative owner next undergoes recursive carrier--polar
exhaustion.  Only a primal--polar fixed joint-saturated atom with an
independent ordinary same-origin realization is a singular mechanism.  With
hypothetical origin it is a prospective source-profile witness; a nonordinary
realization or a polar separator is its next typed successor.  By
\cref{thm:ranked-structural-closure}, the complete iteration ends only in a
finite target-local exclusion or a source-resolved prospective atom with its
origin polarity unchanged.  Thus the protocol asks directly which
target-aligned structural normal form is present; it never begins with a
source-transverse analytic estimate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Finite incidence pruning is \cref{cor:finite-incidence-fast-track}.  Each
normal-form projection is a rational finite-dimensional projection or a
totalized polarity split at depth \(n\).  The invariant definitions are
quadratic-form, order-domination, variation, rank, capacity, circulation, or
graph-feasibility programs, all contained in the finite cylinder-moment
hierarchy.  Soundness gives joint outer boxes.  Exhaustive enumeration,
compactness, retention of all finite correlations, and the five measurement theorems give
\eqref{eq:formation-profile-computation}.  Compactness gives finite detection
of an empty formation-active core.  Compatible nonempty levels reconstruct
a graph-complete cumulative joint point.  The projection theorem exposes
every nonzero limit component on a finite prefix.  After those successors are
processed, the remaining point satisfies \textup{(A1)}--\textup{(A4)}.  Its
realization coordinate is either ordinary, which realizes the structural
atom, or nonordinary, which is the typed proper successor used by
\cref{thm:ranked-structural-closure}.  Hence neither a failed realization
test nor an ordinary path without its joint atom is a terminal label.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[PDE backend]
\label{def:pde-backend}
A \emph{PDE backend} is the homomorphic compilation of a public presentation
into the source, shell, carrier, total-graph, successor, and ordered-relation
signatures used to construct \(\mathfrak G_{\mathfrak b}\).  It may compute
equation-specific coefficients, scaling weights, constraint tails, and
closure edges.  It may not add a source family, a target-relative premise, a
physical measure not generated by the equation, or a terminal declaration
without a proved relation of the ordered algebra.
Here \(\mathfrak G_{\mathfrak b}\) is the induced subgraph of
\(\mathfrak G_A\) obtained by fixing the complete active signature
\(\mathfrak b=(A,m,\Gamma,\eta,\mathbf R)\) and its earlier zero coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Backend conservativity]
\label{prop:backend-conservativity}
Every PDE backend preserves the five-channel normal form, prospective contact
accountability, source-preserving limit closure, the target-null meaning of
\(J_{\rm res}\), and the single physical-budget ledger.  Therefore a backend
can validate or refute regularity only by evaluating the vertices and closure
edges of \(\mathfrak G_{\mathfrak b}\); it cannot change the continuum theory that
generated them.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The backend is a homomorphism into the signature already constructed in
\cref{sec:pde-instantiation}.  Preservation of source normal forms follows
from \cref{thm:part-i-continuum-preservation}; preservation of contact
accountability and the residual quotient follows from
\cref{thm:unconditional-continuum-contact-alternative}; preservation of the
physical ledger follows from signed carrier gluing and
\cref{thm:carrier-physical-budget}.  The prohibited additions are not symbols
of the target signature, so they cannot occur in its image.
\end{proof}

\section{Specialization examples}
\label{sec:stress-test-specializations}

The examples in this section test whether distinct public equations compile
into the same closure calculus.  They are consequences and evaluations of
the general theory.  No example supplies a premise used by
\cref{thm:ranked-structural-closure} or changes its source alphabet, physical
ledger, successor semantics, or terminal alternatives.  In particular, the
Navier--Stokes calculation below has the role of a specialization example,
just as LPN does in Part~I; it is not part of the definition or proof of the
continuum calculus.

\begin{proposition}[Specialization noninterference]
\label{prop:specialization-noninterference}
For every public PDE presentation \(\mathfrak P\), specialization is the
homomorphic substitution
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:pde-specialization-homomorphism}
 \mathsf{Compile}_{\rm cont}(\mathfrak P)
 \longrightarrow
 \bigl(I_{\mathfrak b},\mathscr W_{\mathfrak b},
       \mathcal E_{\mathfrak b},\mathcal K_{\mathfrak b},
       \mathfrak G_{\mathfrak b}\bigr)
\end{equation}
for its reachable active branches.  The definitions and proofs of the
record-scale selector, dual-carrier grammar, compactness routing, modulation
conjugation, selector-accountability closure, and ranked closure theorem are
independent of \(\mathfrak P\).  A backend computes only the images of its
equation, source operators, native carrier, constraints, symmetries, and
target-shell covectors.  It cannot add a branch premise or alter a closing
rule.  Hence every backend example has the same logical status as an
application of the saturated calculus of Part~I.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
All objects on the right of
\eqref{eq:pde-specialization-homomorphism} are functorial constructions from
the public weak equation: ideal generation, adjoint closure, chart pullback,
signed gluing, target quotient, ordered completion, and total-graph
completion.  The general theorems quantify over these generated objects and
contain no equation-specific coefficient.  Substitution therefore preserves
their identities and alternatives.  Backend conservativity
\cref{prop:backend-conservativity} excludes every additional source,
physical ledger, or target-relative premise.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Specialization example: three-dimensional incompressible
Navier--Stokes}

Consider on \(\mathbb R^3\) or the periodic box
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-public-equation}
 \partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla p=\nu\Delta u+f,
 \qquad \nabla\cdot u=0.
\end{equation}
For the regularity validation take \(f=0\), a smooth divergence-free datum of
finite kinetic energy, and the usual maximal strong branch inside the suitable
weak-solution graph.  The complete continuation target consists of terminal
germs at which that strong branch has no continuation.  This target is
generated by the continuation graph; no blow-up norm or profile is inserted
as target data.

The public backend contains the distributional equation, the divergence-free
rational test core, Galerkin and mollification words, the pressure constraint,
Galilean and parabolic covariance graphs, and the tested kinetic-energy
carrier.  On every ordinary unforced branch the carrier relation is
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-single-physical-budget}
 \frac12\|u(t)\|_2^2+
 \nu\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2\dd s
 +\mu_{\rm suit}(\Omega\times[0,t])
 =\frac12\|u_0\|_2^2,
\end{equation}
where \(\Omega\) denotes the spatial domain and
\(\mu_{\rm suit}\ge0\) is the totalized suitable-energy defect.  This
generates the single physical measure
\[
 \dd\mu_{\rm NS}
 :=\nu|\nabla u|^2\dd x\dd t+\dd\mu_{\rm suit}.
\]
This is the sole budget used below.
Its restriction to a parabolic event is raw physical expenditure.  It becomes
the price of singular-shell progress only after the local energy identity is
restricted to a generated target-active branch, decomposed into the five
source currents, and admitted by \eqref{eq:target-aligned-charge-rule}.

For a rational \(E>0\), denote by \(\mathscr X_{\rm NS}(E)\) the closed
physical stratum generated by
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-rational-physical-stratum}
 \frac12\|u_0\|_2^2\le E,
 \qquad
 \mu_{\rm NS}(\Omega\times[0,T])\le E
 \quad(T<T_*).
\end{equation}
The viscosity is reduced to \(\nu=1\) by the ordinary deterministic scaling
of the unforced equation; retaining \(\nu>0\) as a positive public parameter
gives the same ordered graph.  The number \(E\) indexes level sets of the
single physical ledger and is not a second budget.  Every smooth finite-energy
datum lies in \(\mathscr X_{\rm NS}(E)\) for some rational \(E\).  The finite
target programs below operate uniformly on this stratum: origin-cylinder
values are variables constrained by the public datum class and
\eqref{eq:ns-rational-physical-stratum}, rather than unlisted real
coefficients of the program.

\begin{proposition}[Navier--Stokes public input ledger]
\label{prop:ns-public-input-ledger}
The specialization uses only the following seed relations:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(B\arabic*)}]
\item the distributional momentum equation and incompressibility;
\item the whole-space kinetic-energy inequality and the local suitable-energy
inequality, totalized by their nonnegative defects;
\item the pressure equation
\(-\Delta p=\partial_i\partial_j(u_i u_j)\), modulo functions of time;
\item Galilean covariance, parabolic change of variables, rational cutoffs,
Galerkin approximation, and mollification; and
\item integration by parts on the rational test core and weak lower
semicontinuity of the local \(L^2\) norm.
\end{enumerate}
Target shells, source labels, record scales, the adjoint module, defect
coordinates, production forms, carrier cohomology, joint kernels, and branch
closures are generated after these seeds are inserted.  None belongs to the
input ledger.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Items \textup{(B1)}--\textup{(B3)} are the standard weak and suitable-energy
formulation of \eqref{eq:ns-public-equation}.  Item \textup{(B4)} consists of
algebraic transformations and the declared approximation grammar.  Item
\textup{(B5)} is part of the canonical weak test calculus.  Every later
Navier--Stokes object is defined below by applying the general continuum
constructors to these relations.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Navier--Stokes physical entropy cocycle]
\label{prop:ns-physical-entropy-cocycle}
On an ordinary unforced suitable branch define, for \(0\le s\le t<T_*\),
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-entropy-cocycle}
\mathcal M_{\rm NS}[s,t]
 :=\frac12\|u(s)\|_2^2-\frac12\|u(t)\|_2^2
 =\mu_{\rm NS}(\Omega\times[s,t]).
\end{equation}
using the right-continuous kinetic-energy representative; equivalently, first
define the identity at common Lebesgue times and take its Stieltjes extension.
The totalized defect makes this an equality on every graph value.  It obeys
the cocycle law
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-entropy-cocycle-gluing}
 \mathcal M_{\rm NS}[s,t]
 +\mathcal M_{\rm NS}[t,r]
 =\mathcal M_{\rm NS}[s,r]
 \qquad(s\le t\le r),
\end{equation}
and its localized, moving-chart descendant is the signed covariant carrier
\eqref{eq:ns-covariant-carrier-identity}.  After restriction to the minimal
state \(X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\) of
\cref{def:ns-minimal-target-realization}, only incidence-retained production can
pair with a singular shell.  Such production is charged by
\(\mathcal M_{\rm NS}\) exactly when the local carrier-domination row is
ordinary; every other value is a typed successor.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Subtract \eqref{eq:ns-single-physical-budget} at times \(s\) and \(t\).
Countable additivity of viscous expenditure and the suitable defect gives
\eqref{eq:ns-entropy-cocycle} and
\eqref{eq:ns-entropy-cocycle-gluing}.  Push the local suitable-energy equality
through the moving parabolic chart and test by the localized kinetic carrier
to obtain \eqref{eq:ns-covariant-carrier-identity}.  Target-incidence
compression and the charging rule give the last assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Navier--Stokes active and successor signatures]
\label{def:ns-active-successor-signatures}
A Navier--Stokes active signature is the full framework record
\[
 \mathfrak b=(A,m,\Gamma,1/5,\mathbf R),
\]
together with its ordered list of earlier zero polarity and total-graph
coordinates.  It is \emph{algebraically reachable} when each of its finite
prefixes survives the public ordered relations and the same-origin successor
graph.  This condition is enumerated from the presentation and makes no
reference to an actual singular orbit.  If contact occurs, prospective
accountability places its induced signature in this enumeration.  For
the physical stratum \(\mathscr X_{\rm NS}(E)\), write
\(\mathfrak B_{\rm NS}^{\rm reach}(E)\) for the resulting generated set of
signatures.  For
\(\xi\in\{\mathrm{eq,nl,pr,ext,sc,cyc,ord}\}\), let
\(\mathfrak b^\xi\) be the canonical successor signature obtained by
adjoining ordinary values of every earlier Navier--Stokes interface and the
zero, signed-dyadic, or graph-boundary value of the first interface of type
\(\xi\).  Write \(Z_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b^\xi}\) for its target-local
stratum and \(\mathcal K_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b^\xi}\) for the image of the
general cone \(\mathcal K_{\mathfrak b^\xi}\) under Navier--Stokes
specialization.  These signatures retain the shell family, realization mode,
origin, scale record, and detecting covector; the label \(\xi\) alone never
defines a cell.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Navier--Stokes source and scaling compilation]
\label{prop:ns-source-scaling-compilation}
For \eqref{eq:ns-public-equation}, viscosity has \(\Geom\) ancestry, the
fixed nonlinear transport and pressure-constraint transport have \(\Caus\)
ancestry, Galilean and pressure-constant quotients append \(\Abs\), parabolic
charts and scale motion append \(\Lift\), and exterior or terminal flux
appends \(\Bdry\).  Under
\[
 V(y,s)=r\,u(x_0+ry,t_0+r^2s),
 \qquad P(y,s)=r^2p(x_0+ry,t_0+r^2s),
\]
the viscous physical price satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-viscous-price-scaling}
 \nu\int_{Q_r(x_0,t_0)}|\nabla u|^2\dd x\dd t
 =\nu r\int_{Q_1}|\nabla V|^2\dd y\dd s.
\end{equation}
Hence a normalized dissipation gap alone cannot give a scale-independent
admissible price.  Every finite-expenditure contact cascade is routed to the target-aligned
scale-carrier successor cell.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The source assignments follow directly from the constructor grammar.  For
\eqref{eq:ns-viscous-price-scaling}, use
\(\nabla_xu=r^{-2}\nabla_yV\) and
\(\dd x\dd t=r^5\dd y\dd s\).  The resulting factor is \(r\).  A geometric
scale sequence can have finite sum, so the physical-price theorem routes the
finite branch to zero-price saturation rather than asserting a uniform lower
bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Navier--Stokes target-cyclic module]
\label{def:ns-target-cyclic-module}
Write the moving-frame vector field on divergence-free fields as
\[
 \mathcal N_{a,b}(V)
 :=\nu\Delta V-\mathbf P_\sigma\nabla\!\cdot(V\otimes V)
   +a\Lambda V+b\cdot\nabla V,
\]
where \(\mathbf P_\sigma\) is the Leray projection, interpreted through its
local, harmonic, and exterior total graphs.  Fix an algebraically reachable Navier--Stokes
active branch \(\mathfrak b=(A,m,\Gamma,1/5,\mathbf R)\) and a generated
shell \(\Phi\in\Gamma\).  The raw forward and backward words are generated
on \(X_{\mathfrak b}\); after
\cref{def:ns-minimal-target-realization}, every downstream use is restricted
to \(X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\).  Let
\(\mathscr C^0_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}(\Phi)\) be the rational localization module
generated by \(D\Phi\).  The next level adjoins localizations, derivatives,
chart pullbacks, constraint descents, pressure-tail coordinates, defect
polarizations, the source-adapted carrier and square-completion words whose
native carrier covector is
\(DK_\chi(V)=\chi V\), and the ordinary values of
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-adjoint-linearized-operator}
 \mathcal A^*_{V,a,b}\lambda
 :=\nu\Delta\lambda
   +\mathbf P_\sigma\!\left((V\cdot\nabla)\lambda
                    -(\nabla V)^{\mathsf T}\lambda\right)
   -a(2\lambda+y\cdot\nabla\lambda)-b\cdot\nabla\lambda.
\end{equation}
Iterating this rule and all commutators gives
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-target-cyclic-module}
 \mathscr C^\infty_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}(\Phi)
 :=\overline{\bigcup_{n\ge0}\mathscr C^n_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}(\Phi)}^{\rm cyl}.
\end{equation}
Every derivative in this definition is the total graph of rational
difference quotients.  A failed Leray projection, pressure split,
localization, chart, derivative, or commutator is retained at its first
nonordinary value.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Adjoint image of the Navier--Stokes current]
\label{prop:ns-adjoint-current-image}
On the ordinary divergence-free test core,
\[
 D\mathcal N_{a,b}(V)^*\lambda
 =\mathcal A^*_{V,a,b}\lambda.
\]
Consequently \(\mathscr C^\infty_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}(\Phi)\) is exactly the target-local image of
the general target-cyclic module under the Navier--Stokes specialization
homomorphism.  It is generated by \eqref{eq:ns-public-equation} and \(\Phi\);
no additional multiplier is part of the backend.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Linearization of the nonlinear current in a divergence-free direction \(W\)
gives
\(-\mathbf P_\sigma((W\cdot\nabla)V+(V\cdot\nabla)W)\).
Integration by parts gives
\((V\cdot\nabla)\lambda-(\nabla V)^{\mathsf T}\lambda\).
The Laplacian is self-adjoint, \((b\cdot\nabla)^*=-b\cdot\nabla\), and in
three dimensions
\((1+y\cdot\nabla)^*=-(2+y\cdot\nabla)\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:ns-adjoint-linearized-operator}.  The remaining generators are the
images of localization, quotient, covariance, polarization, and commutator
operations in \cref{def:target-cyclic-covector-module}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Navier--Stokes minimal target-active realization]
\label{def:ns-minimal-target-realization}
Let \(\mathscr R^n_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\) be the forward module generated
from the viscous, nonlinear/pressure, quotient, parabolic-chart, and
exterior-current roots by the operations in the public ledger.  Pair it with
\(\mathscr C^n_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}(\Phi)\) from
\eqref{eq:ns-target-cyclic-module}.  The finite Navier--Stokes incidence core
\(\mathsf M^n_{{\rm NS},\Sigma,\mathfrak b}\) consists exactly of vertices
lying both:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)}]
\item downstream of one of those five roots through the momentum, pressure,
localization, chart, defect, carrier, return, or realization graphs; and
\item upstream of \(D\Phi\) through a nonzero signed pairing, a typed pairing
boundary, or an adjoint/commutator edge.
\end{enumerate}
Its graph-complete diagonal closure is denoted
\(\mathsf M_{{\rm NS},\Sigma,\mathfrak b}\).  In particular, a pressure tail,
Reynolds component, scale current, annular flux, or commutator word is retained
exactly when it lies on such a source--shell path.
Write
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-minimal-target-state-space}
 X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}
 :=X_{\mathfrak b}\cap
   \lvert\mathsf M_{{\rm NS},\Sigma,\mathfrak b}\rvert,
 \qquad
 \mathscr C^{n,\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}
 :=\mathscr C^n_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\big|_{X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}}.
\end{equation}
Likewise set
\(
 \mathcal K^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}
 :=\mathcal K_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}
   \big|_{X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}}.
\)
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Navier--Stokes incidence reduction]
\label{prop:ns-incidence-reduction}
The Navier--Stokes specialization maps the abstract minimal realization onto
the one in \cref{def:ns-minimal-target-realization}:
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-minimal-realization-commutation}
 \mathsf S_{\rm NS}(\mathsf M_{\Sigma,\mathfrak b})
 =\mathsf M_{{\rm NS},\Sigma,\mathfrak b}.
\end{equation}
Restriction to this set preserves the signed carrier identity, scale-balance
row, admitted local-energy price, cycle price, circulation-elimination core,
and every finite target cover.  At finite depth the retained coordinate list
is computed by forward and backward graph search before any Navier--Stokes
moment or localizing matrix is formed.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The forward public constructors specialize to the weak momentum, pressure,
Leray, localization, Galilean, parabolic, carrier, defect, return, and
realization graphs listed above.  The backward constructors specialize to
\eqref{eq:ns-adjoint-linearized-operator} and its localized, constrained, and
polarized descendants by \cref{prop:ns-adjoint-current-image}.  Specialization
preserves their pairing and every first nonordinary value.  It therefore
preserves forward reachability, backward reachability, and their
intersection, proving \eqref{eq:ns-minimal-realization-commutation}.  The
remaining assertions are the specialized commutation identities of
\cref{thm:minimal-realization-compiler-commutation}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Navier--Stokes atomic formation vector]
\label{def:ns-atomic-formation-vector}
For \(C\subset X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\), apply the five ordered
normal-form projections to the localized moving equation and its total
graphs.  Denote the resulting specialized tuples by
\[
 \mathfrak I_{{\rm NS},\Sigma}^{c}(C)
 :=\mathsf S_{\rm NS}\!\left(\mathfrak I_{\Sigma}^{c}(C)\right),
 \qquad c\in\Channels.
\]
Concretely, their coordinates are generated as follows.
\begin{longtable}{p{.12\linewidth}p{.78\linewidth}}
\toprule
Source & Navier--Stokes target-aligned normal-form coordinates\\
\midrule
\(\Geom\) &
target projection of the localized Stokes form; Dirichlet
capacity/resistance; target-visible kernel of the Stokes form; first
nonordinary viscous-domain or form-closure value\\
\(\Caus\) &
the signed glued convection--pressure--moving-frame current modulo
coboundaries; exact storage; carrier-domination radius; first-return cycle
price; compressed resolvent response; first nonordinary return or gluing
value\\
\(\Abs\) &
Leray/pressure descent defect; gradient and Galilean vertical component;
pressure-quotient cokernel; first nonordinary incompressibility, pressure,
gauge, or quotient value; kernel capacity and target rank\\
\(\Lift\) &
parabolic-chart intertwining and fiber currents; target-projected Reynolds
concentration and oscillation measures; nonexact scale current; first
nonordinary product, chart, localization, or realization value\\
\(\Bdry\) &
oriented exterior and annular flux after internal cancellation; spatial tail
flux; continuation-shell terminal flux; first nonordinary trace or exhaustion
value; exterior-tail capacity\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
For each nonempty \(A\subseteq\Channels\), define
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-formation-profile}
 \mathfrak F_{{\rm NS},A}^{\Sigma_{\rm sing}}(E)
 :=\mathsf S_{\rm NS}
   \bigl(\mathfrak F_A^{\Sigma_{\rm sing}}(E)\bigr).
\end{equation}
Every entry is a value or total-graph coordinate of the public ledger in
\cref{prop:ns-public-input-ledger}; the table is a compilation rule, not
additional analytic input.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Navier--Stokes normal-form stress test]
\label{thm:ns-normal-form-stress-test}
The Navier--Stokes specialization commutes with all five atomic
normal-form projections and their finite primal--dual invariant programs.
Consequently,
\begin{multline}
 \label{eq:ns-formation-profile-exhaustion}
 \Reach_{\Sigma_{\rm sing}}^{\Phys}(E)>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists\,\varnothing\ne A\subseteq\Channels:\\
 \mathsf{Atom}_{{\rm NS},\Sigma}^{\rm real}(E)
 \text{ contains an atom with source support }A.
\end{multline}
At refinement depth \(n\), the program first computes
\(\mathsf M^n_{{\rm NS},\Sigma,\mathfrak b}\), then computes only the atomic
coordinates in the preceding table whose source--shell incidence paths
survive.  Thus a prospective singularity is attacked by an exhaustive list
of the particular geometric, directed, quotient, lift/scale, and boundary
structures it uses; no global estimate on a source-transverse
Navier--Stokes class is requested.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The Stokes form, signed nonlinear/pressure current, Leray and gauge
quotients, parabolic charts and weak-product completion, and oriented
exterior/terminal graphs are respectively the images of the five public
source constructors.  By
\cref{prop:ns-incidence-reduction}, specialization also preserves the
minimal target realization.  It preserves orthogonal form projection,
closed coboundary projection, horizontal--vertical splitting, the fixed
evaluation compactification, oriented boundary cancellation, total graphs,
and every target pairing.  It therefore commutes with the five ordered
normal forms.  Their invariant programs use only addition, pairing,
quadratic forms, order domination, finite variation, rank, capacity,
circulation, and total-graph feasibility, all preserved by the
specialization homomorphism.  Apply
\cref{thm:continuum-target-structure-exhaustion,%
thm:direct-continuum-invariant-protocol} to obtain
\eqref{eq:ns-formation-profile-exhaustion} and the finite-depth assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Navier--Stokes ordinary-orbit realization and joint-reentry row]
\label{def:ns-ordinary-orbit-realization-gate}
Fix a rational physical stratum \(\mathscr X_{\rm NS}(E)\).  The
\emph{ordinary-orbit realization relation} is the total graph of the map
which sends an ordinary Navier--Stokes path to all coordinates used by the
target compiler.  Its ordinary range, denoted
\(\mathsf{Real}_{\rm NS}(E)\), consists exactly of records
\[
 (u_0,u,p,T_*,\mu_{\rm NS},\mathbf R,
   \operatorname{pol}_{\rm org}(\mathbf R),
   (\Phi_r)_{r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}})
\]
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(G\arabic*)}]
\item \(u_0\) is an actual smooth divergence-free finite-energy datum in
  the origin fiber carried by \(\mathbf R\), and \(u\) is its actual maximal
  strong path in the declared continuation class on \([0,T_*)\).
\item The pair \((u,p)\) has the public weak regularity, satisfies
  \eqref{eq:ns-public-equation} and incompressibility against every rational
  test, and satisfies the pressure graph modulo its time-dependent gauge.
\item The whole-space and localized suitable-energy relations hold with the
  same nonnegative measure \(\mu_{\rm NS}\), and
  \eqref{eq:ns-rational-physical-stratum} holds.
\item Every localization, product, pressure split, quotient, parabolic chart,
  moving-frame equation, signed carrier, return, and successor coordinate in
  the record is the value of the corresponding public operation on this same
  path and origin.
\end{enumerate}
These four rows are generated relations, rather than additional backend
data.  They are ordered after the source, carrier, scale, target-cyclic, and
same-origin rows, and after recursive carrier-polar fixedness for every
cumulative owner.  A record failing that prerequisite returns to the polar
successor queue and is not evaluated by the ordinary-orbit relation.  The
next generated row evaluates the totalized
continuation and shell-contact status of the same ordinary path.  If a record
is not in the ordinary range, the first nonordinary value of this total graph
retains its source support, target covector, physical ledger, origin, and
preceding coordinates and becomes the next \(\mathrm{ord}\)-headed
realization successor.  Write \(\mathsf{Cont}_{T_*}(R)=0\) for the
noncontinuation value and \(\mathsf{Cof}_{\Sigma}(R)=1\) precisely when
\[
 \sup_{t<T_*}\Phi_r(u(t))=1
 \quad\text{for every member of a cofinal generated shell family.}
\]
Define
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-real-singular-set}
 \mathsf{Sing}_{\rm NS}^{\rm real}(E)
 :=\left\{R\in\mathsf{Real}_{\rm NS}(E):
 \operatorname{pol}_{\rm org}(R)=\mathsf{Ind},\
 T_*<\infty,\ \mathsf{Cont}_{T_*}(R)=0,\
 \mathsf{Cof}_{\Sigma}(R)=1\right\}.
\end{equation}
A moment functional, invariant measure, equality kernel, compatible family
of finite boxes, or graph-boundary value is not an element of
\(\mathsf{Sing}_{\rm NS}^{\rm real}(E)\) unless its diagonal record lies in this
ordinary range.
Define the realized Navier--Stokes structural-atom set by
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-realized-structural-atom-set}
 \mathsf{Atom}_{{\rm NS},\Sigma}^{\rm real}(E)
 :=\left\{(R,\mathfrak a):
 \begin{array}{l}
 R\in\mathsf{Sing}_{\rm NS}^{\rm real}(E),\\
 \mathfrak a=\mathsf S_{\rm NS}(\mathfrak a_0)
 \text{ satisfies \textup{(A1)}--\textup{(A4)}, and }R
 \text{ realizes }\mathfrak a
 \end{array}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Thus the realization row verifies the public path and then rejoins its shell,
source, carrier, pressure, scale, and successor coordinates with the complete
cumulative record.  Membership in
\(\mathsf{Sing}_{\rm NS}^{\rm real}(E)\) alone is not a compiler terminal.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact realization and joint-reentry alternative]
\label{thm:ns-realization-gate-alternative}
Fix rational \(E>0\).  Let \(Z\) be a target-active graph-complete
Navier--Stokes record in \(\mathscr X_{\rm NS}(E)\) produced by
the recurrent compiler and fixed under the primal--polar recursion of
\cref{thm:ns-carrier-polar-recursion}.  Exactly one of the following occurs after forming
its cumulative joint record:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(R\arabic*)}]
\item the ordinary realization is target-null, continuable, or lacks the
  cofinal continuation-shell value, so the putative contact cell closes;
\item the least nonordinary realization coordinate is a proper
  target-aligned successor, to which projection-first saturation and the
  recurrent compiler are reapplied;
\item the realization is an ordinary contacting path, and joint reprojection
  exposes a least unprocessed target-aligned increment on a finite cumulative
  prefix; that five-channel component, with the union of its ancestry, is the next
  proper successor;
\item the realization is an ordinary contacting path, its cumulative record
is fixed under every generated joint operation, and its origin polarity is
\(\mathsf{Hyp}\); the output is a saturated Navier--Stokes prospective
source-profile witness;
\item the realization is an ordinary contacting path, its cumulative record
is fixed under every generated joint operation, and its origin polarity is
\(\mathsf{Ind}\); the output is the independently realized structural atom
  \((Z,\mathfrak a)\in
    \mathsf{Atom}_{{\rm NS},\Sigma}^{\rm real}(E)\).
\end{enumerate}
In particular, a formal target-spine record, compatible inverse limit, or
ordinary singular path without its fixed source-resolved joint atom is never
a terminal Navier--Stokes output, and a contact-derived path is never an
independent singular-existence output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Totalize the four ordinary-orbit rows of
\cref{def:ns-ordinary-orbit-realization-gate} in their fixed order, followed
by the continuation and shell-contact row.  If the first four values are
ordinary, the origin row gives one actual datum and one actual same-origin
path.  Density of the rational test core gives the distributional equation,
incompressibility, and pressure relation; the carrier graph gives the
suitable-energy relations and the physical measure.  If the final row has a
target-null or continuable value, this is \textup{(R1)}.  If one of the first
four ordinary values fails, the
first-failure theorem assigns the corresponding typed graph coordinate and
its inherited source.
Projection-first saturation retains it precisely when its target pairing is
nonzero.  This is the proper successor in \textup{(R2)}.

It remains to consider an ordinary contacting value.  Rejoin its complete
ordinary path record with all earlier compiler states and apply
\cref{thm:continuum-composition-no-creation}.  A nonzero target component on
a finite joint prefix gives \textup{(R3)} exactly when it is unprocessed.  If
every increment is processed, joint closure either creates a new increment,
again giving \textup{(R3)}, or the maximal cumulative record is fixed under all generated operations and
retains \(A_{\Phi,N}=N\), the five-source identity, and the single physical
measure.  These are \textup{(A1)}--\textup{(A4)}.  Origin polarity is a
closed discrete coordinate.  Its \(\mathsf{Hyp}\) value gives the source
profile witness in \textup{(R4)}.  Its \(\mathsf{Ind}\) value places the
ordinary path in \(\mathsf{Sing}_{\rm NS}^{\rm real}(E)\) and realizes the
atom in \textup{(R5)}.  If the complete joint projection were target-null,
it would contradict the cofinal unit shell rows.  The five cases are disjoint
and exhaustive.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Executable Navier--Stokes formation transition]
\label{def:ns-executable-formation-transition}
Fix rational \(E>0\).  Let \(C\) be a target-visible cell in
\(\mathfrak F_{{\rm NS},A}^{\Sigma_{\rm sing}}(E)\).  Expand its atomic
formation vector only after joining \(C\) with its complete predecessor
transcript and saturating every generated mixed coordinate.  Then process the
result in the order
\(\Geom,\Caus,\Abs,\Lift,\Bdry\), retaining simultaneous nonzero entries in
the support \(A\).  The next transition is determined by the first row below
whose detector has not already been resolved.
\begin{longtable}{p{.11\linewidth}p{.29\linewidth}p{.48\linewidth}}
\toprule
Head & Target-local detector & Generated transition\\
\midrule
\(\Geom\) & Stokes range, kernel, capacity, or form-graph value &
ordinary range production enters the local carrier-domination graph; a
positive admitted value is charged, an unabsorbed signed value enters
feeding/circulation, and a kernel or nonordinary form value is the next
target-cyclic or typed successor\\
\(\Caus\) & glued convection--pressure current, storage, cohomology,
response, or return value & exact coboundaries cancel; positive cycle price
closes by physical charge; zero cycle price restricts to its circulation
support; nonzero storage, cohomology, or return value becomes the next
signed-dyadic successor\\
\(\Abs\) & Leray/pressure descent, vertical class, cokernel, target descent,
or quotient-graph value & a zero descended class is removed in the target
quotient; every nonzero target rank or cokernel is processed by the quotient
capacity and target-cyclic rows; a failed descent is the corresponding typed
successor\\
\(\Lift\) & chart intertwining, fiber current, Reynolds concentration,
oscillation, scale current, or lift-graph value & fixed-scale zero-price
ordinary values enter the gradient-kernel test; shrinking values enter the
moving-microscope and scale-carrier rows; concentration and oscillation enter
polarized production; a failed chart, product, or scale relation is the next
typed successor\\
\(\Bdry\) & exterior, pressure-tail, terminal, trace, or exhaustion value &
admitted positive exterior input is charged; pressure tails enter the
constraint-tail decomposition; terminal shell motion enters the completed
boundary-current row; every nonordinary trace or exhaustion value is the next
typed successor\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
After these rows, a target-active zero-price value enters circulation and
resaturation.  A normalized circulation selects support and is immediately
rejoined with the unnormalized shell cocycle.  A record reaches the
realization row only after every earlier target-visible detector, every mixed
joint coordinate, and every generated descendant has been resolved.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[No unclassified Navier--Stokes formation cell]
\label{thm:ns-no-unclassified-formation-cell}
Fix rational \(E>0\).  Every formation-active point of every one of the
thirty-one profiles
\(\mathfrak F_{{\rm NS},A}^{\Sigma_{\rm sing}}(E)\) has exactly one next
framework transition:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(N\arabic*)}]
\item a local ordered identity makes its target projection zero or excludes
  its public equation cell;
\item an admitted local carrier identity charges its target return to the
  single physical measure;
\item the least nonzero or nonordinary detector in
  \cref{def:ns-executable-formation-transition}, including a component
  exposed by a finite cumulative joint prefix, produces a proper
  target-aligned successor; or
\item every finite joint increment is source-resolved, the cumulative record
  is fixed under the complete generated closure, and the ordinary realization
  row has hypothetical origin; it produces the saturated Navier--Stokes
  source-profile witness;
\item the same fixed ordinary realization has independent origin and produces
  a member of \(\mathsf{Atom}_{{\rm NS},\Sigma}^{\rm real}(E)\).
\end{enumerate}
The first two are closing transitions, the third is recursive, the fourth is
the prospective source-profile output, and the fifth is the only singular
terminal.  An ordinary contacting path that has not
passed joint saturation returns to the third transition.  No
profile point, positive functional, invariant law, equality kernel, or target
spine is an additional output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The five normal-form rows are exhaustive by
\cref{thm:ns-normal-form-stress-test}.  Their zero, positive ordinary,
signed-dyadic, and graph-boundary values are precisely the transitions in
\cref{def:ns-executable-formation-transition}.  The local charging rule
permits physical expenditure only in \textup{(N2)}.  Projection-first
saturation and source-preserving completion assign every remaining nonzero
value to \textup{(N3)} with its complete ancestry.  Resolved-prefix
monotonicity makes each finite successor proper.  If such successors continue
cofinally, \cref{thm:continuum-composition-no-creation} reapplies the
five-channel projection to their cumulative join.  Its nonzero finite-prefix
component is again \textup{(N3)}, while a target-null limit closes in
\textup{(N1)}.  If no new coordinate remains, the ordinary-orbit realization
graph is the next generated row and
\cref{thm:ns-realization-gate-alternative} gives \textup{(N1)},
\textup{(N3)}, the hypothetical profile witness \textup{(N4)}, or the
independently realized atom \textup{(N5)}.  Hence the list is
exhaustive and has no target-visible residual case.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Target-active Navier--Stokes Hamiltonian response]
\label{def:ns-target-active-hamiltonian-response}
On an ordinary point of
\(X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\), let
\begin{align}
 H_{\rm NS}W&:=-\nu\mathbf P_\sigma\Delta W,
 \label{eq:ns-target-hamiltonian}\\
 A_{V,a,b}W
 &:=-\mathbf P_\sigma\bigl((V\cdot\nabla)W+(W\cdot\nabla)V\bigr)
   +a\Lambda W+b\cdot\nabla W,
 \label{eq:ns-target-directed-linearization}\\
 L_{V,a,b}&:=-H_{\rm NS}+A_{V,a,b}.
 \label{eq:ns-target-linearized-generator}
\end{align}
The divergence-free and pressure quotients are included in the generated
\(\Abs\) graph.  Let \(P_{\mathscr I}\) be the cylinder projection onto the
retained forward source words and let \(P_{\mathscr O}\) be the cylinder
projection onto the retained target-cyclic covectors.  At an ordinary
resolvent point define
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-target-active-resolvent}
 \Psi_{{\rm NS},\Sigma}(\lambda;V,a,b)
 :=\left\|P_{\mathscr O}
       (\lambda-L_{V,a,b})^{-1}P_{\mathscr I}\right\|.
\end{equation}
The resolvent, its norm epigraph, and its input/output projections are
total-graph coordinates.  Their first nonordinary values are target-cyclic
successors with the ancestry of the operation that failed.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Compressed Navier--Stokes resolvent factorization]
\label{prop:ns-compressed-resolvent-factorization}
The response \eqref{eq:ns-target-active-resolvent} is the Navier--Stokes
specialization of \eqref{eq:target-active-full-resolvent} after minimal
incidence reduction.  For every retained source variation \(K^c\), its
ordinary derivative is
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-resolvent-source-factorization}
 P_{\mathscr O}(\lambda-L)^{-1}
 K^c(\lambda-L)^{-1}P_{\mathscr I}.
\end{equation}
Consequently every target-visible pseudospectral amplification factors
through a retained \(\Geom\), \(\Caus\), \(\Abs\), \(\Lift\), or \(\Bdry\)
word.  If the resolvent relation, pressure descent, domain identification, or
input/output projection is nonordinary, its typed value is the next incidence
edge.  At finite depth, only matrix elements indexed by
\(\mathsf M^n_{{\rm NS},\Sigma,\mathfrak b}\) enter the ordered target
program.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The Stokes form is the \(\Geom\) part of the specialized generator;
linearized convection is fixed \(\Caus\), the Leray and pressure graphs are
\(\Abs\), chart velocity is \(\Lift\), and exterior domain values are
\(\Bdry\).  Compression by \(P_{\mathscr I}\) and
\(P_{\mathscr O}\) is exactly the source--target incidence restriction.
Apply \cref{prop:nonnormal-source-invariance} on the ordinary resolvent graph
to obtain \eqref{eq:ns-resolvent-source-factorization}.  Source-preserving
totalization supplies every listed boundary value.  The finite statement is
\cref{cor:finite-incidence-fast-track} under Navier--Stokes specialization.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Navier--Stokes generated productions]
\label{def:ns-generated-productions}
For
\(\lambda\in\mathscr C^{\infty,\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}(\Phi)\),
pair the moving equation
with every rational localization of \(\lambda\), glue common faces, and
complete every algebraic square.  The resulting production cone
\(\mathscr P_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}(\Phi)\) is the least closed positive cone containing
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)}]
\item for rational \(0\le\chi\le1\),
\[
 D_\chi(V)=\nu\int\chi^2|\nabla V|^2,
 \qquad
 M^{(r)}_\chi
 =r^{-1}\int\chi^2\!\left(\frac{x-x_0}{r},
                    \frac{t-t_0}{r^2}\right)\dd\mu_{\rm suit}(x,t);
\]
\item the positive Reynolds-defect polarizations generated by weak limits of
\(V\otimes V\);
\item the Dirichlet forms
\(\Gamma_{\nu,\chi}(\lambda)=\nu\int|\nabla(\chi\lambda)|^2\)
and every commutator square generated from \(\nu\Delta\),
\(\mathcal A^*_{V,a,b}\), rational localization, and the Leray constraint;
and
\item positive boundary or scale terms only when the signed carrier identity
proves that positivity after all compatible faces have been glued.
\end{enumerate}
Each member retains the source word of the expansion that generated it.
Only members dominated by \(\mu_{\rm NS}|_Q\) through the target-local signed
carrier identity are admissible physical charges for the selected shell
event.  All other members are joint-kernel or carrier-domination successor
coordinates.  Define
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-target-cyclic-joint-kernel}
 X^\infty_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b,\Phi}
 :=X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\cap
   \bigcap_{P\in\mathscr P_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}(\Phi)}\{P=0\}.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Navier--Stokes defect polarization]
\label{prop:ns-defect-polarization}
Let \(V_k\rightharpoonup V\) in \(L^2_{\rm loc}\) along a total-graph
sequence in the minimal target-active stratum
\(X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\).  Exactly one of the
following occurs: the tensor coordinate has a first nonordinary value,
producing the nonlinear successor
\(Z_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b^{\rm nl}}\); or it has an ordinary weak measure value and
\[
 \mathcal R_{ij}
 :=\mathrm{w\!\!\!-lim}_k(V_k)_i(V_k)_j-V_iV_j
\]
is positive semidefinite in the sense that
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-reynolds-defect-positive}
 \int\chi\,\zeta_i\mathcal R_{ij}\zeta_j\ge0
 \qquad(\chi\ge0, \zeta\in\mathbb Q^3)
\end{equation}
for every rational compactly supported cutoff.  Its pressure descendant is
the total solution of
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-defect-pressure}
 -\Delta q_{\mathcal R}=\partial_i\partial_j\mathcal R_{ij},
\end{equation}
split into local singular-integral, harmonic, and exterior coordinates.
Thus a nonlinear weak defect yields a positive production coordinate and its
signed \(\Caus/\Abs/\Bdry\) descendants.  Failure of the tensor limit or of
any pressure coordinate is the corresponding first-failure successor.
The production coordinate is not thereby declared to be physical
expenditure: on the active branch it is charged to \(\mu_{\rm NS}\) only if
the target-local signed carrier factorization proves the domination row
\eqref{eq:target-aligned-charge-rule}.  A nonordinary domination value is
retained in the carrier successor coordinate of the same signature.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For fixed \(\chi\) and \(\zeta\), weak lower semicontinuity of the
\(L^2(\chi\dd y\dd s)\) norm gives
\[
 \int\chi|\zeta\cdot V|^2
 \le\liminf_k\int\chi|\zeta\cdot V_k|^2,
\]
which is \eqref{eq:ns-reynolds-defect-positive}.  Rational polarization
determines the symmetric tensor coordinate.  Taking the divergence of the
weak momentum equation gives \eqref{eq:ns-defect-pressure}; the standard
local Poisson decomposition gives the three displayed descendants.  The
total graph supplies their boundary values without a convergence premise.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Navier--Stokes prospective contact compiler]
\label{thm:ns-prospective-contact-compiler}
If an ordinary finite-energy Navier--Stokes branch contacts the complete
continuation target, then it generates pairwise disjoint pre-contact events
\(Q_j\), normalized shell records \(R_j\), and sourcewise currents such that
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-unit-contact-current}
 \Delta\widehat\phi(R_j)=1,
 \qquad
 \begin{cases}
  \sum_{c\in\Channels}Q_{c,j}=1,
  \quad\max_{c\in\Channels}Q_{c,j}^{+}\ge1/5,
      &\text{for finite current totals},\\
  \overline Q^{o_j}_{j}(1)\ge1/5,
      &\text{on a variation-boundary value}.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
After passage to a subsequence one nonempty support
\(A\subseteq\Channels\), one realization mode, and one same-origin cascade
record occur for every \(j\), producing the active signature
\(\mathfrak b=(A,m,\Gamma,1/5,\mathbf R)\).  The residual current has
zero pairing with every shell differential and cannot occur in \(A\).
Moreover
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-disjoint-physical-price}
 \sum_j\mu_{\rm NS}(Q_j)
 \le \mu_{\rm NS}(\mathbb R^3\times(0,T_*))
 \le \frac12\|u_0\|_2^2.
\end{equation}
The quantities in \eqref{eq:ns-disjoint-physical-price} are raw event
expenditures.  They are admissible prices for the sourcewise shell currents
only on the ordinary carrier-domination value of the target-local fact
normal form; every other value is retained as a successor of
\(\mathfrak b\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \cref{thm:deterministic-prospective-accountability} to the generated
finite-cylinder shells and then
\cref{thm:canonical-disjoint-shell-cascade}.  Source preservation under
continuum completion is \cref{thm:source-preserving-completion}, and the
target-null residual statement is
\eqref{eq:zero-saturated-residual-source}.  Since there are five sources, the
finite affine identity or closed owner in
\eqref{eq:ns-unit-contact-current} gives the floor \(1/5\), and finite
source and realization-mode exhaustion gives the constant-signature
subsequence.  Countable
additivity of the measure in \eqref{eq:ns-single-physical-budget} gives
\eqref{eq:ns-disjoint-physical-price}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Scale-aware Navier--Stokes expenditure record]
\label{def:ns-scale-aware-expenditure}
For a parabolic event \(Q_r(x_0,t_0)\), write
\begin{align}
 D_R(V)&:=\nu\int_{Q_R}|\nabla V|^2\,\dd y\dd s,\\
 M_{r,R}&:=r^{-1}\mu_{\rm suit}
 \bigl(Q_{rR}(x_0,t_0)\bigr),\\
 p_{r,R}&:=\mu_{\rm NS}\bigl(Q_{rR}(x_0,t_0)\bigr),
\end{align}
and retain \(r,D_R,M_{r,R}\) as separate graph coordinates.  The raw
event-expenditure coordinate satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-scale-price-product}
 p_{r,R}=r\bigl(D_R(V)+M_{r,R}\bigr).
\end{equation}
The product relation, rather than either factor separately, belongs to the
physical carrier ideal.  Its use as target price additionally requires the
local charging relation for the selected shell current.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Exact fixed-scale closure]
\label{lem:ns-fixed-scale-closure}
Let a zero-event-expenditure Navier--Stokes successor law be supported on a stratum
\(r\ge r_*>0\).  Then it is supported on
\(D_R=M_{r,R}=0\) for every rational \(R\).  Its ordinary weak-equation component
is spatially constant.  It is zero on \(\mathbb R^3\) under finite energy and
is constant modulo the Galilean quotient on the periodic box.  Hence its
ordinary target projection vanishes.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:ns-scale-price-product}, nonnegativity, and
\(r\ge r_*\) give
\[
 D_R+M_{r,R}\le r_*^{-1}p_{r,R}=0.
\]
An exhaustion by rational cylinders gives \(\nabla V=0\) distributionally.
The weak fundamental theorem on connected domains makes \(V\) spatially
constant, as in \cref{cor:gradient-kernel-equality-reduction}.  A spatial
constant in \(L^2(\mathbb R^3)\) is zero; on the periodic box it is removed
by the generated Galilean quotient.  Such states lie in
\(\Null_{\Sigma_{\rm sing}}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Scale-collapse degeneracy is algebraic]
\label{lem:ns-scale-collapse-degeneracy}
On the closed stratum \(r=0\), the physical-price relation
\eqref{eq:ns-scale-price-product} imposes no upper bound on \(D_R+M_{r,R}\).
Consequently zero physical price alone cannot activate
\cref{cor:gradient-kernel-equality-reduction} on a parabolically normalized
singular cascade.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
In the ordered coordinate algebra the relation becomes
\(p_{0,R}=0\cdot(D_R+M_{0,R})=0\).  For a sequential realization, choose any
\(d_n\ge0\), put \(r_n=(n(1+d_n))^{-1}\), and set
\(D_R(V_n)+M_{r_n,R}=d_n\).  Then
\(r_n\to0\) and \(p_{r_n,R}\le n^{-1}\to0\), while \(d_n\) is arbitrary.
Thus no inequality \(D_R+M_R\le C p_{r,R}\) with scale-independent \(C\)
is a consequence of the carrier relation.  The failure is the vanishing
coefficient of a displayed equation.  It activates the covariant microscope
below; it is not an endpoint of the structural calculation.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Covariant parabolic microscope]
\label{def:ns-covariant-microscope}
Let \(r(\tau)>0\) and \(x(\tau)\in\mathbb R^3\) be absolutely continuous and
choose physical time by
\[
 \dot t(\tau)=r(\tau)^2.
\]
For \(y=(x-x(\tau))/r(\tau)\), set
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-moving-chart}
 V(y,\tau)=r(\tau)u(x(\tau)+r(\tau)y,t(\tau)),
 \qquad
 P(y,\tau)=r(\tau)^2p(x(\tau)+r(\tau)y,t(\tau)),
\end{equation}
and write
\[
 a=\frac{\dot r}{r},\qquad b=\frac{\dot x}{r},\qquad
 \Lambda V=V+y\cdot\nabla V.
\]
The coordinates \((a,b)\) are chart velocities, not additional controls and
not additional physical expenditure.  Their currents retain \(\Lift\)
ancestry and the ancestry of the equation transported by the chart.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Exact moving-microscope equation]
\label{prop:ns-moving-microscope-equation}
On every ordinary part of the solution graph, the fields in
\eqref{eq:ns-moving-chart} satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-moving-frame-equation}
 \partial_\tau V+(V\cdot\nabla)V+\nabla P
 =\nu\Delta V+a\Lambda V+b\cdot\nabla V,
 \qquad \nabla\cdot V=0.
\end{equation}
On a boundary value of any displayed operation, the same formula holds in
the total graph with the corresponding typed boundary current.  Thus passage
to a collapsing scale does not discard the normalized equation: it adds the
explicit scale and translation currents in \eqref{eq:ns-moving-frame-equation}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate \eqref{eq:ns-moving-chart}, use \(\dot t=r^2\), and substitute
\eqref{eq:ns-public-equation}.  The derivatives of the amplitude, dilation,
and center are respectively \(aV\), \(ay\cdot\nabla V\), and
\(b\cdot\nabla V\).  The spatial divergence is preserved by the chart.
Totalization commutes with this algebraic calculation by
\cref{thm:source-preserving-completion}; a failed product, derivative,
pressure, or chart relation is therefore retained with its typed ancestry.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Signed covariant kinetic carrier]
\label{thm:ns-signed-covariant-carrier}
Let \(\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)\) be nonnegative and independent of
\(\tau\), and put
\[
 e=\frac{|V|^2}{2},\qquad K_\phi(V)=\int e\phi,
 \qquad
 D_\phi=\nu\int |\nabla V|^2\phi.
\]
The pushed-forward suitable-energy defect defines a nonnegative Stieltjes
measure \(\dd M_\phi\), and the exact local carrier identity is
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-covariant-carrier-identity}
 \dd K_\phi+D_\phi\,\dd\tau+\dd M_\phi
 =\bigl(F_{\rm int,\phi}+F_{\rm sc,\phi}
       +F_{\rm tr,\phi}\bigr)\dd\tau,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align}
 F_{\rm int,\phi}
  &=\int(e+P)V\cdot\nabla\phi
    +\nu\int e\,\Delta\phi,\label{eq:ns-internal-carrier-current}\\
 F_{\rm sc,\phi}
  &=-a\int e(\phi+y\cdot\nabla\phi),
  \label{eq:ns-scale-carrier-current}\\
 F_{\rm tr,\phi}
  &=-\int e\,b\cdot\nabla\phi.
  \label{eq:ns-translation-carrier-current}
\end{align}
The three terms are signed currents.  In particular, neither
\(F_{\rm sc,\phi}^{+}\) nor \(|F_{\rm sc,\phi}|\) is declared to be physical
expenditure.  Scale motion is first glued with the other oriented currents;
only the surviving nonexact scale current enters the target-active carrier
cohomology.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Test \eqref{eq:ns-moving-frame-equation} against \(V\phi\).  Incompressibility
gives the convection and pressure contribution in
\eqref{eq:ns-internal-carrier-current}; integration by parts gives the
viscous terms.  In dimension three,
\[
 \int V\cdot\Lambda V\,\phi
 =-\int e(\phi+y\cdot\nabla\phi),
 \qquad
 \int V\cdot(b\cdot\nabla V)\phi
 =-\int e\,b\cdot\nabla\phi.
\]
The local suitable inequality becomes equality after adjoining its
nonnegative defect measure.  This proves
\eqref{eq:ns-covariant-carrier-identity}.  The last assertion is exactly the
signed gluing order of \cref{thm:signed-carrier-gluing}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[No free shrinkage]
\label{prop:ns-no-free-shrinkage}
Fix an algebraically reachable active signature
\(\mathfrak b=(A,m,\Gamma,1/5,\mathbf R)\), and let
\(\Phi\in\Gamma\) be a generated differentiable target-shell observable in
the moving chart.  Along an ordinary chart interval in
\(X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\),
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-covariant-shell-current}
 \frac{\dd}{\dd\tau}\Phi(V)
 =D\Phi(V)\!\left[
 \nu\Delta V-(V\cdot\nabla)V-\nabla P
 +a\Lambda V+b\cdot\nabla V\right],
\end{equation}
and the total-graph version holds without differentiability by the derived
Stieltjes current.  Hence a unit shell crossing in a shrinking chart still
has total source pairing one.  After quotienting target-null translations
and gluing internal faces, if the \(\Geom\), \(\Caus\), \(\Abs\), and
\(\Bdry\) pairings vanish, then the nonexact \(\Lift\) scale current has
positive target pairing.  Shrinkage can move target progress into the scale
channel; it cannot erase that progress or place it in \(J_{\rm res}\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Equation \eqref{eq:ns-covariant-shell-current} is the chain rule applied to
\eqref{eq:ns-moving-frame-equation}.  On a nonordinary value it is the
definition of the derived shell current, so all first failures remain in the
five-source sum.  Integrating over a normalized crossing interval gives
increment one.  Signed gluing cancels exact internal and chart coboundaries.
The target-local fact factorization keeps every term in the full signature
\(\mathfrak b\).  The residual is target-null, so the asserted scale pairing
is forced by the remaining equality; no statement about a current outside
  \(X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\) is used.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Scale-cell gluing and microscope passivity]
\label{thm:ns-microscope-passivity}
Let \(C_0,\ldots,C_N\) be consecutive target-retaining parabolic cells from
one physical Navier--Stokes orbit, with compatible centers, scales, cutoffs,
and overlap orientations, all in one active signature \(\mathfrak b\).
Restrict each local-energy relation to
\(X^{\min}_{{\rm NS},\mathfrak b}\), apply the
five-source fact normal form, and sum
\eqref{eq:ns-covariant-carrier-identity} before taking positive parts gives
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-scale-cell-gluing}
 K_N+\sum_{j<N}(D_j+M_j)
 =K_0+I_{{\rm ext},N}+H_{{\rm sc},N}.
\end{equation}
Here \(D_j=\int_{C_j}D_\phi\,\dd\tau\),
\(M_j=M_\phi(C_j)\), and \(K_0,K_N\) are the oriented root and leaf
carrier values.
Here paired convection, pressure, cutoff, translation, and exact scale
currents telescope; \(I_{{\rm ext},N}\) is the genuine exterior
\(\Bdry\) input, and \(H_{{\rm sc},N}\) is the nonexact scale-carrier class.
After totalization, every infinite recurrent target-retaining chain has
exactly one of the following generated continuations:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item a compactness, realization, pressure, overlap, exterior-tail, chart, or
carrier relation has a first nonordinary value, which produces its typed
target-active successor;
\item all preceding coordinates are ordinary, the exterior current either
cancels in the coherent complex or satisfies the target-local charging rule
for the public orbitwise carrier, and the
aggregate carrier has a strict block deficit
\(D+M-F_{\rm sc}\ge\delta>0\), which is incompatible with bounded
\(K_\phi\) and \eqref{eq:ns-scale-cell-gluing};
\item all preceding coordinates are ordinary and a stationary target-aligned
moving-microscope law satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:ns-scale-saturation-law}
 \int(F_{\rm sc}-D-M)\,\dd\varpi=0
\end{equation}
and all same-origin successor relations.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the ordinary scale-collapse branch is reduced to the equality law
\eqref{eq:ns-scale-saturation-law}; it is not a branch on which normalized
dissipation becomes unobservable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Apply \cref{thm:signed-carrier-gluing} to each finite compatible subcomplex.
It gives \eqref{eq:ns-scale-cell-gluing} and identifies its two noninternal
terms.  Totalize compactness, realization, pressure, overlap, exhaustion,
chart, and carrier gluing in that order.  Their least nonordinary value gives
\textup{(i)}.  On the ordinary graph, common faces cancel.  A remaining
  exterior current either satisfies the target-local carrier domination or is
  its typed \(\Bdry\) coordinate, already covered by \textup{(i)}.  Apply
\cref{thm:strict-passivity-or-saturation} to the resulting recurrent law.
In the strict alternative every retained block lowers the bounded carrier by
